change_log.area: Add user fetching and printing functionality
change_log.old_code: main.py did not exist (or was empty), providing no user fetching or printing functionality.
change_log.new_code: main.py defines get_user(user_id) that performs a GET request to https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/{user_id}, returns JSON on status 200 else prints "Something went wrong" and returns None; print_user(user_id) calls get_user and prints the user's name and email; the script's entry point calls print_user(999).
change_log.impact: Enables fetching and displaying user name and email from an external API, but introduces risk of crashes if get_user returns None or missing keys, lacks timeout/retry mechanisms, uses a hardcoded endpoint, and provides minimal error handling.

post_review.title: Dereferencing None returned from get_user causes crash
post_review.body: In print_user, the variable user is assigned the result of get_user without checking if it is None. When get_user returns None (non‑200 status or network error), the subsequent lines user["name"] and user["email"] raise a TypeError, causing the script to abort unexpectedly.

post_review.title: Missing timeout on HTTP request can lead to indefinite hanging
post_review.body: The call to requests.get(url) does not specify a timeout parameter. If the remote service is slow or unresponsive, the function will block forever, affecting responsiveness and potentially causing resource exhaustion in larger applications.

post_review.title: No exception handling for network or JSON parsing errors
post_review.body: get_user only checks the status code; it does not catch requests.exceptions (e.g., ConnectionError, Timeout) or json.JSONDecodeError. Such exceptions propagate unhandled, crashing the program and obscuring the root cause.

post_review.title: Hardcoded endpoint, use of print for errors, and lack of documentation/type hints
post_review.body: The URL is hardcoded, reducing flexibility for testing or environment changes. Errors are communicated via print statements instead of logging, which limits configurability. Additionally, the functions lack docstrings and type annotations, making the code harder to maintain and understand.

post_review_verdict: The new code introduces a critical bug where print_user will crash if get_user fails, and it lacks basic robustness measures such as timeouts, exception handling, and input validation. While the functionality is straightforward, these issues must be addressed before merging to ensure reliability and maintainability. Fix the None check, add a timeout, wrap the request in a try/except block, and consider making the endpoint configurable and using logging instead of print. After these changes, the code will be ready for merge.

bug_findings.title: print_user may raise KeyError/TypeError on None or missing keys
bug_findings.detail: print_user calls get_user and directly accesses user["name"] and user["email"] without checking if user is None or if the keys exist, which can raise KeyError or TypeError on non‑200 responses or malformed JSON.
bug_findings.fix: Add a check for user being None and use .get() with appropriate defaults or handle missing data gracefully.

bug_findings.title: HTTP request lacks timeout
bug_findings.detail: requests.get is invoked without a timeout, which can cause the program to hang indefinitely if the remote service is unresponsive or slow.
bug_findings.fix: Add a timeout argument, e.g., requests.get(url, timeout=5).

bug_findings.title: Hardcoded external API URL
bug_findings.detail: The URL is hardcoded, reducing flexibility and requiring code changes if the endpoint changes.
bug_findings.fix: Make the URL configurable via a function argument, environment variable, or configuration file.
